claim: Human telomerase RNA (hTR) biological stability relies on H/ACA proteins.
source: Biological stability of human telomerase RNA (hTR) relies on H/ACA proteins, but other eukaryotes use other RNP assembly pathways.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known fact about hTR.

claim: Other eukaryotes use RNP assembly pathways different from H/ACA proteins for telomerase RNA stability.
source: Biological stability of human telomerase RNA (hTR) relies on H/ACA proteins, but other eukaryotes use other RNP assembly pathways.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about eukaryotic diversity in telomerase assembly.

claim: Minimized hTR with only binding sites for TERT assembled biologically active enzyme.
source: Remarkably, with only binding sites for telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), minimized hTR assembled biologically active enzyme.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: TERT overexpression was required for cellular interaction with minimized hTR.
source: TERT overexpression was required for cellular interaction with minimized hTR, indicating that H/ACA RNP assembly enhances endogenous hTR-TERT interaction.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing that hTRmin required TERT OE for activity.

claim: H/ACA RNP assembly enhances endogenous hTR-TERT interaction.
source: TERT overexpression was required for cellular interaction with minimized hTR, indicating that H/ACA RNP assembly enhances endogenous hTR-TERT interaction.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that TERT OE was required for hTRmin but not for wild-type hTR.

claim: Telomere maintenance by minimized telomerase was unaffected by elimination of TCAB1.
source: Telomere maintenance by minimized telomerase was unaffected by the elimination of the telomerase holoenzyme Cajal body chaperone TCAB1 or the Cajal body scaffold protein Coilin.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing stable telomere length in TCAB1 KO cells with hTRmin.

claim: Telomere maintenance by minimized telomerase was unaffected by elimination of Coilin.
source: Telomere maintenance by minimized telomerase was unaffected by the elimination of the telomerase holoenzyme Cajal body chaperone TCAB1 or the Cajal body scaffold protein Coilin.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing stable telomere length in Coilin KO cells with hTRmin.

claim: Wild-type hTR maintained and elongated telomeres in TCAB1 knockout cells.
source: Surprisingly, wild-type hTR also maintained and elongated telomeres in TCAB1 or Coilin knockout cells, with distinct changes in telomerase action.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing telomere maintenance in TCAB1 KO cells.

claim: Wild-type hTR maintained and elongated telomeres in Coilin knockout cells.
source: Surprisingly, wild-type hTR also maintained and elongated telomeres in TCAB1 or Coilin knockout cells, with distinct changes in telomerase action.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing telomere maintenance in Coilin KO cells.

claim: Eukaryotic chromosome stability relies on end-protective telomeres.
source: Eukaryotic chromosome stability relies on end-protective telomeres (Arnoult and Karlseder, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: End-protective telomeric chromatin assembles on a tract of simple-sequence DNA repeats in most organisms.
source: In most organisms, end-protective telomeric chromatin assembles on a tract of simple-sequence DNA repeats (de Lange, 2010), for example the human repeat of TTAGGG on the strand with 3'OH terminus.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The human telomeric repeat is TTAGGG on the strand with 3'OH terminus.
source: In most organisms, end-protective telomeric chromatin assembles on a tract of simple-sequence DNA repeats (de Lange, 2010), for example the human repeat of TTAGGG on the strand with 3'OH terminus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about human telomeres.

claim: Maintenance of telomeric repeat array requires de novo repeat synthesis by telomerase.
source: Maintenance of this telomeric repeat array requires de novo repeat synthesis by the ribonucleoprotein (RNP) reverse transcriptase telomerase to balance the repeat erosion inherent in DNA-dependent DNA-polymerase replication of the genome (Blackburn et al., 2006; Hug and Lingner, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Telomerase extends chromosome 3' ends by copying a template within the telomerase RNA subunit.
source: Telomerase extends chromosome 3' ends by copying a template within the telomerase RNA subunit (hTR in human cells), using an active site in the telomerase reverse transcriptase protein (TERT).
evidence: This is established knowledge about telomerase mechanism.

claim: Ciliate, fungal, and vertebrate telomerases follow entirely different RNP biogenesis pathways.
source: Curiously, ciliate, fungal, and vertebrate telomerases follow entirely different RNP biogenesis pathways, which are directed by telomerase RNA interaction with a La-motif protein, Sm proteins, or H/ACA proteins, respectively (Egan and Collins, 2012a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Ciliate telomerase RNP biogenesis is directed by telomerase RNA interaction with a La-motif protein.
source: Curiously, ciliate, fungal, and vertebrate telomerases follow entirely different RNP biogenesis pathways, which are directed by telomerase RNA interaction with a La-motif protein, Sm proteins, or H/ACA proteins, respectively (Egan and Collins, 2012a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Fungal telomerase RNP biogenesis is directed by telomerase RNA interaction with Sm proteins.
source: Curiously, ciliate, fungal, and vertebrate telomerases follow entirely different RNP biogenesis pathways, which are directed by telomerase RNA interaction with a La-motif protein, Sm proteins, or H/ACA proteins, respectively (Egan and Collins, 2012a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Vertebrate telomerase RNP biogenesis is directed by telomerase RNA interaction with H/ACA proteins.
source: Curiously, ciliate, fungal, and vertebrate telomerases follow entirely different RNP biogenesis pathways, which are directed by telomerase RNA interaction with a La-motif protein, Sm proteins, or H/ACA proteins, respectively (Egan and Collins, 2012a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Human telomerase shares the same mature H/ACA proteins (dyskerin, NHP2, NOP10, GAR1) as intron-encoded small nucleolar or small Cajal body RNPs.
source: In human cells, telomerase shares the same mature H/ACA proteins (dyskerin, NHP2, NOP10, GAR1) and H/ACA RNP biogenesis chaperones as the intron-encoded small nucleolar (sno) or small Cajal body (sca) RNPs that catalyze cleavage and pseudouridylation of ribosomal and small nuclear RNAs (Kiss et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Precursor hTR is released from its site of synthesis as an autonomous transcript rather than the spliced intron lariat of other human H/ACA RNAs.
source: Because precursor hTR is released from its site of synthesis as an autonomous transcript rather than the spliced intron lariat of other human H/ACA RNAs, it is sensitized to degradation in dyskeratosis congenita (DC) patient cells with a mutation of an H/ACA protein (Egan and Collins, 2012b; Armanios and Blackburn, 2012; Sarek et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: hTR is sensitized to degradation in dyskeratosis congenita patient cells with a mutation of an H/ACA protein.
source: Because precursor hTR is released from its site of synthesis as an autonomous transcript rather than the spliced intron lariat of other human H/ACA RNAs, it is sensitized to degradation in dyskeratosis congenita (DC) patient cells with a mutation of an H/ACA protein (Egan and Collins, 2012b; Armanios and Blackburn, 2012; Sarek et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: hTR requires a 5' trimethylguanosine cap to prevent 5'-3' exonuclease processing.
source: Also, unlike other H/ACA RNAs, hTR requires a 5' trimethylguanosine cap to prevent 5'-3' exonuclease processing (Mitchell et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: RNP trafficking from nucleoli to steady-state concentration in Cajal bodies depends on the binding of TCAB1 to an hTR 3' stem-loop CAB-box motif.
source: Subsequent RNP trafficking from nucleoli to steady-state concentration in Cajal bodies depends on the binding of the Cajal body chaperone and telomerase holoenzyme protein TCAB1/WDR79/WRAP53β to an hTR 3' stem-loop CAB-box motif (Venteicher et al., 2009; Tycowski et al., 2009; Zhong et al., 2011), which is present in both stem-loops of an H/ACA scaRNA (Kiss et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Transient telomere colocalization with a Cajal body can be detected in S-phase.
source: Transient telomere colocalization with a Cajal body can be detected in S-phase, when telomerase acts at chromosome ends (Jády et al., 2006; Tomlinson et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Telomerase acts at chromosome ends in S-phase.
source: Transient telomere colocalization with a Cajal body can be detected in S-phase, when telomerase acts at chromosome ends (Jády et al., 2006; Tomlinson et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TCAB1 or Coilin depletion using RNA interference reduced or eliminated hTR colocalization with telomeres and induced telomere shortening.
source: Evidence for Cajal body delivery of telomerase to telomeres builds from studies depleting TCAB1 or Coilin using RNA interference, which reduced or eliminated hTR colocalization with telomeres and induced telomere shortening (Venteicher et al., 2009; Zhong et al., 2011; Stern et al., 2012; Zhong et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: DC patient cells with biallelic TCAB1 mutations have short telomeres.
source: DC patient cells with biallelic TCAB1 mutations have short telomeres and fail to maintain telomere length even with the up-regulated telomerase expression in induced pluripotent cells (Batista et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: DC patient cells with biallelic TCAB1 mutations fail to maintain telomere length even with up-regulated telomerase expression in induced pluripotent cells.
source: DC patient cells with biallelic TCAB1 mutations have short telomeres and fail to maintain telomere length even with the up-regulated telomerase expression in induced pluripotent cells (Batista et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Mouse telomerase RNA does not localize to Cajal bodies.
source: With all of this experimental support for Cajal body delivery of human telomerase to telomeres, it is puzzling that mouse telomerase RNA does not localize to Cajal bodies (Tomlinson et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Coilin gene knock-out in HeLa cells generated two clonal cell lines that maintained telomeres.
source: Also, recently, Coilin gene knock-out (KO) in HeLa cells generated two clonal cell lines that maintained telomeres (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: hTRmin containing only binding sites for TERT can assemble active RNP in cells.
source: Remarkably, we found that a minimal hTR (hTRmin) containing only binding sites for TERT can assemble active RNP in cells, and this active RNP can maintain stable telomere length homeostasis.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: hTRmin active RNP can maintain stable telomere length homeostasis.
source: Remarkably, we found that a minimal hTR (hTRmin) containing only binding sites for TERT can assemble active RNP in cells, and this active RNP can maintain stable telomere length homeostasis.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing stable telomere lengths over time.

claim: hTR H/ACA RNP assembly enhances TERT interaction at scarce endogenous telomerase subunit levels.
source: TERT overexpression was required for cellular assembly with hTRmin, suggesting that hTR H/ACA RNP assembly enhances TERT interaction at scarce endogenous telomerase subunit levels.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that TERT OE was required for hTRmin but not for wild-type hTR.

claim: KO of TCAB1 or Coilin did not alter hTRmin RNP function at telomeres.
source: KO of TCAB1 or Coilin did not alter hTRmin RNP function at telomeres.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing stable telomere maintenance in KO cells.

claim: TCAB1 KO was permissive for hTR telomerase to maintain telomeres.
source: Surprisingly, TCAB1 KO or Coilin KO was also permissive for hTR telomerase to maintain telomeres.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing telomere maintenance in TCAB1 KO cells.

claim: Coilin KO was permissive for hTR telomerase to maintain telomeres.
source: Surprisingly, TCAB1 KO or Coilin KO was also permissive for hTR telomerase to maintain telomeres.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing telomere maintenance in Coilin KO cells.

claim: In cancer and pluripotent stem cell lines with endogenous hTR and TERT expression, TCAB1 KO resulted in a slow decline of telomere length followed by stable telomere length homeostasis.
source: In cancer and pluripotent stem cell lines with endogenous hTR and TERT expression, TCAB1 KO resulted in a slow decline of telomere length followed by stable telomere length homeostasis.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing telomere length dynamics in TCAB1 KO cells.

claim: hTR assembly as H/ACA RNP is not essential aside from conferring hTR stability and facilitating active telomerase assembly in cells with scarce TERT.
source: We conclude that aside from conferring hTR stability and facilitating active telomerase assembly in cells with scarce TERT, hTR assembly as H/ACA RNP is not essential.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings with hTRmin.

claim: Cajal body localization is not essential for hTRmin or hTR telomerase to maintain stable telomere length homeostasis.
source: Also, Cajal body localization is not essential for hTRmin or hTR telomerase to maintain stable telomere length homeostasis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings with TCAB1 and Coilin KO cells.

claim: The H/ACA-motif 5' stem of hTR separates two hTR regions that are critical for binding of TERT and catalytic activity: the template/pseudoknot (t/PK) and conserved regions (CR) 4/5.
source: The H/ACA-motif 5' stem of hTR (Figure 1A) separates two hTR regions that are critical for binding of TERT and catalytic activity: the template/pseudoknot (t/PK) and conserved regions (CR) 4/5 (Zhang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: hTRmin in combination with TERT reconstitutes a minimized active telomerase in rabbit reticulocyte lysate.
source: Previously we joined these two regions with a spacer to create hTRmin (Figure 1B), which in combination with TERT reconstitutes a minimized active telomerase in rabbit reticulocyte lysate (Wu and Collins, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Appending 3' processing and protection motifs from the human long non-coding RNA MALAT1 allowed cellular accumulation of hTRmin.
source: To allow cellular accumulation of hTRmin, the most successful strategy was to append 3' processing and protection motifs from the human long non-coding RNA MALAT1 (Brown et al., 2012; 2014).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citations to prior work on MALAT1.

claim: Cellular hTRmin accumulation required both the RNA triplex and the RNase P site.
source: Accumulation of hTRmin to a level detectable by Northern blot required both the RNA triplex and the RNase P site (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Cellular reconstitution with hTRmin yielded lower RNA accumulation and proportionally lower overall activity than reconstitution with hTR.
source: Cellular reconstitution with hTRmin yielded lower RNA accumulation and proportionally lower overall activity than reconstitution with hTR, but hTRmin and hTR telomerase RNPs had similar profiles of repeat synthesis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: hTRmin and hTR telomerase RNPs had similar profiles of repeat synthesis.
source: Cellular reconstitution with hTRmin yielded lower RNA accumulation and proportionally lower overall activity than reconstitution with hTR, but hTRmin and hTR telomerase RNPs had similar profiles of repeat synthesis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TERT, dyskerin, and TCAB1 each bound hTR whereas only TERT bound LhTRmin.
source: As expected, TERT, dyskerin, and TCAB1 each bound hTR whereas only TERT bound LhTRmin.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunopurification experiments shown in Figure 1F.

claim: LhTRmin accumulated to a level lower than endogenous hTR when stably expressed from an integrated transgene.
source: Stably expressed hTRmin was barely detectable, and even LhTRmin accumulated to a level lower than endogenous hTR (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: The MALAT1 3' processing elements do not confer as much accumulation to minimized hTR as does an embedded H/ACA RNP.
source: Therefore, the MALAT1 3' processing elements do not confer as much accumulation to minimized hTR as does an embedded H/ACA RNP.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing hTRmin and LhTRmin accumulation to endogenous hTR.

claim: hTR concentrated in nuclear puncta while LhTRmin distributed throughout the nucleoplasm.
source: While hTR concentrated in nuclear puncta as expected, LhTRmin distributed throughout the nucleoplasm (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from FISH shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Two independent HCT116 cell lines with homozygous TERC KO lacked telomerase catalytic activity in cell extract.
source: Two independent cell lines with homozygous TERC KO were confirmed to lack telomerase catalytic activity in cell extract, as assayed by the PCR-based telomeric repeat amplification protocol performed with radiolabeled dGTP (hotTRAP) (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, left).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: hTR KO clonal HCT116 cell lines initially showed no growth defect.
source: Initially, these two hTR KO clonal cell lines showed no growth defect.
evidence: This is an observation from the study.

claim: Transgene expression of wild-type hTR restored telomerase catalytic activity to the hTR KO cells.
source: Transgene expression of wild-type hTR restored telomerase catalytic activity to the hTR KO cells, rescuing endogenous TERC locus disruption (Figure 2D, lane 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: LhTRmin or hTRmin with TERT OE generated active telomerase in hTR KO cells.
source: However, LhTRmin or hTRmin with TERT OE did generate active telomerase (Figure 2D, lanes 7–8).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: TERT co-expression did not affect hTRmin biological accumulation.
source: TERT co-expression did not affect hTRmin biological accumulation (Figure 2D, compare lanes 4–5 to lanes 7–8).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: hTR assembly as H/ACA RNP strongly stimulates hTR interaction with TERT when both subunits are at very low expression levels.
source: From these experiments we conclude that hTR assembly as H/ACA RNP strongly stimulates hTR interaction with TERT when both subunits are at very low expression levels, but this role of H/ACA RNP assembly can be bypassed by increasing the cellular availability of TERT.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that TERT OE was required for hTRmin but not for wild-type hTR.

claim: The role of H/ACA RNP assembly in stimulating hTR-TERT interaction can be bypassed by increasing the cellular availability of TERT.
source: From these experiments we conclude that hTR assembly as H/ACA RNP strongly stimulates hTR interaction with TERT when both subunits are at very low expression levels, but this role of H/ACA RNP assembly can be bypassed by increasing the cellular availability of TERT.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that TERT OE was required for hTRmin but not for wild-type hTR.

claim: hTR KO cell lines lacking active telomerase entered an interval of pervasive cell death at ~70 days post-targeting.
source: The hTR KO cell lines lacking active telomerase ultimately entered an interval of pervasive cell death with dramatic membrane blebbing (Figure 2E, yellow arrowheads) at ~70 days post-targeting, corresponding to ~70 population doublings.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and microscopy images shown in Figure 2E.

claim: All telomerase-positive polyclonal cell cultures and clonal cell lines proliferated over many months of continuous passage with normal morphology and doubling time.
source: In stark contrast, all of the telomerase-positive polyclonal cell cultures and clonal cell lines proliferated over many months of continuous passage with normal morphology and doubling time (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Catalytically active hTRmin telomerase RNPs conferred indefinite cellular proliferative capacity.
source: Therefore, the catalytically active hTRmin telomerase RNPs conferred indefinite cellular proliferative capacity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that telomerase-positive cells proliferated indefinitely.

claim: hTR KO cells re-expressing hTR rapidly gained telomere length.
source: As expected, hTR KO cells re-expressing hTR rapidly gained telomere length, whereas hTR KO cells expressing the negative control GFP did not (Figure 3A, lanes 1–3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: All cell cultures lacking active telomerase had short telomeres that continued to shorten until eventually all cells in the culture died.
source: All cell cultures lacking active telomerase had short telomeres that continued to shorten until eventually all cells in the culture died (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: Clonal cell lines from hTR KO cells complemented by LhTRmin or hTRmin with TERT OE had distinct but stable telomere lengths.
source: These clonal cell lines had distinct but stable telomere lengths (Figure 3C,D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C, 3D, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: All of the LhTRmin cell lines had higher steady-state RNA accumulation than the hTRmin lines.
source: All of the LhTRmin cell lines had higher steady-state RNA accumulation than the hTRmin lines (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Higher telomerase activity in cell extract correlated generally but not absolutely to longer telomere length at homeostasis.
source: Higher telomerase activity in cell extract correlated generally but not absolutely to longer telomere length at homeostasis (compare Figure 3F, bars to Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing Figure 3F and Figure 3C.

claim: hTRmin telomerase RNP assembled in the stable cell lines did not have the endogenous hTR RNP interaction with TCAB1.
source: We confirmed that the hTRmin telomerase RNP assembled in the stable cell lines did not have the endogenous hTR RNP interaction with TCAB1, tested by immunopurification of TCAB1 from cell lysate and subsequent telomerase activity assay (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TCAB1 KO cells retained a normal level of Coilin, and Coilin KO cells retained a normal level of TCAB1.
source: TCAB1 KO cells retained a normal level of Coilin, and Coilin KO cells retained a normal level of TCAB1 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Cells lacking TCAB1 retained Cajal bodies.
source: Cells lacking TCAB1 retained Cajal bodies (Figure 4C), in agreement with some previous findings (Venteicher et al., 2009; Zhong et al., 2011) but contrary to others (Mahmoudi et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and citations to prior work.

claim: Nuclear foci of SMN remained detectable in the TCAB1 KO cells but not Coilin KO cells.
source: Also, nuclear foci of SMN remained detectable in the TCAB1 KO cells but not Coilin KO cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In HCT116 cells, TCAB1 KO did not disrupt Cajal bodies.
source: We conclude that in HCT116 cells, TCAB1 KO did not disrupt Cajal bodies, and Coilin KO did not induce TCAB1 degradation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunofluorescence and immunoblot data.

claim: In HCT116 cells, Coilin KO did not induce TCAB1 degradation.
source: We conclude that in HCT116 cells, TCAB1 KO did not disrupt Cajal bodies, and Coilin KO did not induce TCAB1 degradation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunofluorescence and immunoblot data.

claim: Clonal cell lines with homozygous TCAB1 or Coilin KO retained telomerase catalytic activity in cell extract.
source: These clonal cell lines retained telomerase catalytic activity in cell extract (Figure 4E) and stably maintained telomeres (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Clonal cell lines with homozygous TCAB1 or Coilin KO stably maintained telomeres.
source: These clonal cell lines retained telomerase catalytic activity in cell extract (Figure 4E) and stably maintained telomeres (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Neither TCAB1 KO nor Coilin KO affected cell viability, morphology, or proliferation in a readily detectable manner.
source: Importantly, neither TCAB1 KO nor Coilin KO affected cell viability, morphology, or proliferation in a readily detectable manner.
evidence: This is an observation from the study.

claim: An RNP of minimized hTRmin and TERT functions at telomeres without dependence on H/ACA RNP biogenesis or localization pathways.
source: These findings support the conclusion that an RNP of minimized hTRmin and TERT functions at telomeres without dependence on H/ACA RNP biogenesis or localization pathways.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings with hTRmin in TCAB1 and Coilin KO cells.

claim: The loss of TCAB1 or Coilin did not alter telomerase activity in cell extract by more than a few-fold extent that could be within the range of clonal variation.
source: The loss of TCAB1 or Coilin did not alter telomerase activity in cell extract by more than a few-fold extent that could be within the range of clonal variation (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: HCT116 cells with TCAB1 KO or Coilin KO showed no change in growth rate, cell viability, or morphology over more than half a year of continuous culture.
source: HCT116 cells with TCAB1 KO or Coilin KO showed no change in growth rate, cell viability, or morphology over more than half a year of continuous culture.
evidence: This is an observation from the study.

claim: TERT KO HCT116 cells underwent cell death at ~70 days after targeting.
source: In contrast, the TERT KO cells underwent cell death at ~70 days after targeting, paralleling the fate of the hTR KO HCT116 cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: TERT KO cells experienced rapid, progressive telomere attrition.
source: As expected the TERT KO cells experienced rapid, progressive telomere attrition (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Telomeres shortened more gradually in the TCAB1 KO clonal cell lines, followed by stable telomere length homeostasis.
source: Surprisingly, telomeres shortened more gradually in the TCAB1 KO clonal cell lines, followed by stable telomere length homeostasis (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: After more than half a year of continuous growth, telomere lengths in all of the TCAB1 KO clonal cell lines stabilized at a few kbp shorter than telomeres in the parental cell line.
source: The starting point of telomere length in TCAB1 KO clonal cell lines mirrored the amount of telomerase activity in cell extract (compare Figure 5D and Figure 5F, left panel), but after more than half a year of continuous growth, telomere lengths in all of the TCAB1 KO clonal cell lines stabilized at a few kbp shorter than telomeres in the parental cell line (Figure 5F, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Telomeres in Coilin KO clonal cell lines cultured in parallel remained near the length of telomeres in the parental HCT116 cells.
source: In comparison, telomeres in Coilin KO clonal cell lines cultured in parallel remained near the length of telomeres in the parental HCT116 cells (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: In HCT116 cells, neither TCAB1 nor Coilin is required for a stable telomere length homeostasis.
source: We conclude that in HCT116 cells, neither TCAB1 nor Coilin is required for a stable telomere length homeostasis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings with TCAB1 and Coilin KO cells.

claim: hESC lines lacking TCAB1 or Coilin were viable with no evident change in cell morphology or proliferation.
source: As observed for HCT116 cells, hESC lines lacking TCAB1 or Coilin were viable with no evident change in cell morphology or proliferation.
evidence: This is an observation from the study.

claim: Neither TCAB1 KO nor Coilin KO affected telomerase activity assayed in hESC cell extract beyond the range of clonal variation.
source: Neither TCAB1 KO nor Coilin KO affected telomerase activity assayed in cell extract beyond the range of clonal variation (Figure 5I and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5I and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Over many months of continuous culture, hESCs lacking TCAB1 experienced very gradual telomere shortening followed by telomere length maintenance.
source: Over many months of continuous culture, hESCs lacking TCAB1 experienced very gradual telomere shortening followed by telomere length maintenance (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5J.

claim: The rate of telomere shortening in TCAB1 KO hESCs was slow compared to telomere shortening in TERT KO hESC.
source: The rate of telomere shortening was slow compared to telomere shortening in TERT KO hESC (Sexton et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior work supported by a citation.

claim: hESCs lacking Coilin retained telomere lengths comparable to the parental hESC culture.
source: The hESCs lacking Coilin retained telomere lengths comparable to the parental hESC culture (Figure 5K).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5K.

claim: TCAB1 KO HCT116 cells ectopically expressing F-tagged TCAB1 regained telomere length.
source: TCAB1 KO HCT116 cells ectopically expressing F-tagged TCAB1 regained telomere length (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3A,B.

claim: TCAB1 KO hESCs ectopically expressing F-tagged TCAB1 regained telomere length.
source: Likewise, TCAB1 KO hESCs ectopically expressing F-tagged TCAB1 regained telomere length (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3C,D.

claim: Cells with homozygous disruptions of TCAB1 exon 2 and exon 8 showed no proliferation defect.
source: Cells with homozygous disruptions of exon 2 and exon 8 showed no proliferation defect, no change in telomere length from the exon 2 KO, and no loss of Cajal bodies (Figure 5—figure supplement 3F,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3F,G.

claim: Cells with homozygous disruptions of TCAB1 exon 2 and exon 8 showed no change in telomere length from the exon 2 KO.
source: Cells with homozygous disruptions of exon 2 and exon 8 showed no proliferation defect, no change in telomere length from the exon 2 KO, and no loss of Cajal bodies (Figure 5—figure supplement 3F,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3F,G.

claim: Cells with homozygous disruptions of TCAB1 exon 2 and exon 8 showed no loss of Cajal bodies.
source: Cells with homozygous disruptions of exon 2 and exon 8 showed no proliferation defect, no change in telomere length from the exon 2 KO, and no loss of Cajal bodies (Figure 5—figure supplement 3F,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3F,G.

claim: TCAB1 and Cajal bodies are not essential for hTR telomerase to maintain telomeres at a stable length homeostasis.
source: Overall, based on the assays described above, we conclude that TCAB1 and Cajal bodies are not essential for hTR telomerase to maintain telomeres at a stable length homeostasis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings with TCAB1 and Coilin KO cells.

claim: The parental, TCAB1 KO, and Coilin KO HCT116 cells with integrated hTR and TERT transgenes acquired ~2-fold elevated hTR and ~5-fold elevated telomerase catalytic activity.
source: The parental, TCAB1 KO, and Coilin KO HCT116 cells with integrated hTR and TERT transgenes acquired ~2-fold elevated hTR and ~5-fold elevated telomerase catalytic activity (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Telomere elongation was rapid in TCAB1 KO HiT cell cultures, reaching the limit of length discrimination almost immediately.
source: Telomere elongation was rapid in TCAB1 KO HiT cell cultures, reaching the limit of length discrimination almost immediately.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Rapid telomere elongation in TCAB1 KO cells is consistent with telomere elongation in wild-type HeLa cells by overexpression of CAB-box-mutant hTR.
source: Rapid telomere elongation in TCAB1 KO cells is consistent with telomere elongation in wild-type HeLa cells by overexpression of CAB-box-mutant hTR (Fu and Collins, 2007; Cristofari et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior work supported by citations.

claim: Coilin KO HiT cells had less telomere elongation compared to TCAB1 KO HiT cells.
source: In comparison, Coilin KO HiT cells had less telomere elongation (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: If telomerase is abundant, TCAB1 is not required to support telomerase-mediated elongation of even relatively long telomeres.
source: We conclude that if telomerase is abundant, TCAB1 is not required to support telomerase-mediated elongation of even relatively long telomeres.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings with HiT cells.

claim: Human telomerase H/ACA RNP assembly is essential for the biological stability of hTR.
source: Integrating all of the findings of this study, we conclude that human telomerase H/ACA RNP assembly is essential not only for the biological stability of hTR but also for active RNP biogenesis at scarce subunit expression levels.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Human telomerase H/ACA RNP assembly is essential for active RNP biogenesis at scarce subunit expression levels.
source: Integrating all of the findings of this study, we conclude that human telomerase H/ACA RNP assembly is essential not only for the biological stability of hTR but also for active RNP biogenesis at scarce subunit expression levels.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: H/ACA RNP assembly gives endogenous-level hESC telomerase the ability to maintain long telomeres.
source: In addition, H/ACA RNP assembly gives endogenous-level hESC telomerase the ability to maintain long telomeres.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings with hESCs.

claim: All H/ACA RNP assembly roles can be bypassed using hTRmin.
source: Remarkably, all of these H/ACA RNP assembly roles can be bypassed using hTRmin (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings with hTRmin.

claim: Stabilization and efficient interaction of low-abundance telomerase subunits is a main rationale for the vertebrate telomerase H/ACA RNP biogenesis pathway.
source: Studies here point to stabilization and efficient interaction of low-abundance telomerase subunits as a main rationale for the vertebrate telomerase H/ACA RNP biogenesis pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: TCAB1 could influence the subnuclear distribution of active RNP between nucleoli and nucleoplasm.
source: As one model to account for these results, TCAB1 could influence the subnuclear distribution of active RNP between nucleoli and nucleoplasm (Figure 7, right).
evidence: This is a speculative model proposed to explain the experimental findings.

claim: TCAB1 KO affected telomere length only in cells with hTR telomerase, not in cells with hTRmin telomerase.
source: However, in studies here it is striking that TCAB1 KO affected telomere length only in cells with hTR telomerase, not in cells with hTRmin telomerase.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing TCAB1 KO effects in hTR vs hTRmin cells.

claim: Coilin KO clonal cell lines generated in this work had telomere lengths similar to the parental cell lines.
source: Coilin KO clonal cell lines generated in this work had telomere lengths similar to the parental cell lines.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Coilin KO cells with endogenous telomerase levels have apparently unperturbed telomere length homeostasis.
source: Because Coilin KO cells with endogenous telomerase levels have apparently unperturbed telomere length homeostasis, we suggest that they will be useful for visually tracking telomerase interactions with telomeres without the complication of Cajal body clustering of active with inactive hTR.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Coilin KO HCT116 cells had dampened telomere elongation upon an increase in telomerase expression.
source: Curiously, Coilin KO HCT116 cells had dampened telomere elongation upon an increase in telomerase expression.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Endogenous hTR colocalization with telomeres was reduced more by Coilin depletion than TCAB1 depletion in previous studies.
source: For example, opposite the impact of TCAB1 and Coilin KOs on telomere lengths described above, previous studies found that endogenous hTR colocalization with telomeres was reduced more by Coilin depletion than TCAB1 depletion and overexpressed hTR colocalization with telomeres was reduced more by TCAB1 depletion than by Coilin depletion (Zhong et al., 2012; Stern et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Overexpressed hTR colocalization with telomeres was reduced more by TCAB1 depletion than by Coilin depletion in previous studies.
source: For example, opposite the impact of TCAB1 and Coilin KOs on telomere lengths described above, previous studies found that endogenous hTR colocalization with telomeres was reduced more by Coilin depletion than TCAB1 depletion and overexpressed hTR colocalization with telomeres was reduced more by TCAB1 depletion than by Coilin depletion (Zhong et al., 2012; Stern et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TCAB1 mutations result in severe dyskeratosis congenita.
source: Also, TCAB1 mutations result in severe DC (Zhong et al., 2011; Armanios and Blackburn, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TCAB1 mutations reduce telomere length in early human development and in somatic cells with long telomeres.
source: We suggest that TCAB1 mutations reduce telomere length in early human development and in somatic cells with long telomeres.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.
